title: Superposition of water waves (তরঙ্গের উপরিপাতন)
placement: Book pages 192–193, topic 7.2.1 তরঙ্গের বৈশিষ্ট্য, item (v) উপরিপাতন: next to চিত্র ৭.০৩ and the নিজে করো with a plate of water.
description: Superposition of water waves (page 192, topic 7.2.1 (v), চিত্র ৭.০৩) in a real ripple tank on a lab bench: a vibrator bar hung on two helical springs, with a small motor and its eccentric weight, drives two point dippers in step, and each sends circular ripples (f = 5 Hz, v = 0.25 m/s, λ = 5 cm, falling off as 1/√r) across a deep blue water surface computed on the GPU, whose colour follows its height, with pale foam beaches so nothing reflects. Where the waves cancel the water turns a calm grey-blue and faint dashed lines mark the still lines (স্থির রেখা). Two floating corks show the idea: কর্ক ক on the centre line (crest meets crest) bobs twice as high, কর্ক খ on a still line (paths differ by 1½λ: crest meets trough) stays almost still, though each wave alone makes it bob. One row of words (১ম তরঙ্গ · ২য় তরঙ্গ · দুটো একসাথে) and one numbered action walk the three cases; a live চিত্র ৭.০৩ in the panel draws, for each cork, the 1st wave, the 2nd wave and their sum against time; the result line gives the two amplitudes in a, the rule the book's sentence, and a line the book's (ii): amplitude 2a → four times the energy. Waves are drawn 12 times taller and 5 times slower (said on the picture). A quiet pause and start-over. Test tab: 5 questions (crest meets trough, which cork bobs most, one source lifted, a cork's amplitude read off the water, double amplitude gives four times the energy), each wrong choice a real mistake with its own note. Phone-first, Bangla and English.
